title: API keys are easier to manage
summary:
API keys got editable controls, midijourney moved to GPT-5.2, and Enter’s dashboard became easier to navigate.

Existing keys can now be renamed, enabled or disabled, and edited for Pollen budget, model access, account permissions and expiry without deleting them. Text, Image and Video permissions also gained category-level Select all and Deselect all controls.

The midijourney text model now routes to GPT-5.2 while retaining its prompt transform. GPT Image was also moved to a different Azure endpoint.

Balance, usage, pricing and key settings received clearer layouts, including horizontally scrollable pricing tables on narrow screens. Dashboard component cleanup came with a fix for case-sensitive Linux builds and targeted TypeScript checks.

highlights.title: Edit keys without replacing them
highlights.text: Rename an existing API key, enable or disable it, and change its Pollen budget, model access, account permissions or expiry. [Manage API keys](https://enter.pollinations.ai/keys).

highlights.title: Select models by category
highlights.text: When restricting an API key to specific models, select or deselect all Text, Image or Video models at once without changing the other categories. [Manage API keys](https://enter.pollinations.ai/keys).

highlights.title: Midijourney moves to GPT-5.2
highlights.text: The `midijourney` text model now uses GPT-5.2 while keeping its prompt transform. [Explore midijourney](https://enter.pollinations.ai/models?q=midijourney).
